about: Published age-group and sex reference norms, used to place a personal measurement inside its cohort instead of only against the athlete's own baseline. Every block names its source, carries a full citation and a URL, and is flagged primary or secondary. Nothing in this file may be presented as fact without the accompanying source and caveats.

conventions.age_max_null: An age_max of null means the published band is open ended at the top.
conventions.values: Keys are percentile ranks, values are the published measurement at that rank.
conventions.direction: higher_is_better means a larger value sits at a higher percentile. lower_is_better inverts that, so the published table is read from the top down.
conventions.missing_percentiles: A percentile the source did not publish is absent, never filled in by estimation.

vo2max.label: VO2max
vo2max.comparability_note: Garmin reports an estimated VO2max derived from heart rate and pace during running. The FRIEND percentiles come from directly measured oxygen uptake during a maximal cardiopulmonary exercise test. The two are not the same measurement, so a percentile read from this table is an indication of the cohort position, not an exact rank.
caveats: The FRIEND 2022 update reports treadmill values 1.5 to 4.6 mL/kg/min lower than the 2015 standards it replaces. Which edition is used therefore shifts the resulting percentile by several ranks. Both editions ship here so the difference stays visible.

FRIEND is a United States cohort. The 2022 paper states that the standards should be cautiously applied to individuals from locations outside the United States, and that global reference standards are still being developed.

ACSM and Cooper Institute fitness categories (labels such as good, excellent, superior) are a different classification built on a different cohort, in the Cooper case on predicted rather than measured VO2max. They are not interchangeable with FRIEND percentiles and are deliberately not included in this file.
Percentiles are published per decade band. A value is compared against the whole band, so a 30 year old and a 39 year old are measured against the same anchors.

friend_2022_treadmill.name: FRIEND registry, 2022 update, treadmill CPX
friend_2022_treadmill.citation: Kaminsky LA, Arena R, Myers J, Peterman JE, Bonikowske AR, Harber MP, Medina Inojosa JR, Lavie CJ, Squires RW. Updated Reference Standards for Cardiorespiratory Fitness Measured with Cardiopulmonary Exercise Testing: Data from the Fitness Registry and the Importance of Exercise National Database (FRIEND). Mayo Clin Proc. 2022;97(2):285-293. doi:10.1016/j.mayocp.2021.08.020. PMID 34809986. Table 3.
friend_2022_treadmill.access_note: The publisher site returns HTTP 403 to automated requests. The figures here were read from the publisher PDF as archived by the Internet Archive at https://web.archive.org/web/2023id_/https://www.mayoclinicproceedings.org/action/showPdf?pii=S0025-6196%2821%2900645-5 . The article is open access under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.
friend_2022_treadmill.verification: The 50th percentile row was independently confirmed against a secondary rendition at https://www.differenthealth.com/blog/vo2-max-by-age (men 46.5 / 39.7 / 35.3 / 29.2 / 24.6 / 20.6 and women 36.6 / 28.3 / 25.7 / 22.9 / 19.6 / 17.2 across the 20-29 to 70-79 bands), which matches this table exactly.
friend_2022_treadmill.population: 22,379 maximal CPX tests from 34 laboratories in the United States, conducted 1968-01-01 through 2021-03-31, in apparently healthy adults aged 20 to 89 with no known cardiovascular disease and no known chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. This block holds the treadmill subset only: 9,564 tests in men and 6,714 tests in women. Maximal effort was defined as a peak respiratory exchange ratio of at least 1.0.
friend_2022_treadmill.measure: Directly measured peak oxygen uptake (VO2peak) during treadmill cardiopulmonary exercise testing.

friend_2015_treadmill.name: FRIEND registry, original 2015 standards, treadmill CPX
friend_2015_treadmill.citation: Kaminsky LA, Arena R, Myers J. Reference Standards for Cardiorespiratory Fitness Measured With Cardiopulmonary Exercise Testing: Data From the Fitness Registry and the Importance of Exercise National Database. Mayo Clin Proc. 2015;90(11):1515-1523. doi:10.1016/j.mayocp.2015.07.026. PMID 26455884. Table 3, FRIEND rows only.
friend_2015_treadmill.access_note: The publisher site returns HTTP 403 to automated requests. The figures here were read from the free NIH author manuscript deposited at PubMed Central (PMC4919021, NIHMS794790), fetched as structured XML through the NCBI E-utilities efetch endpoint.
friend_2015_treadmill.verification: Two independent extractions of the same deposit, one from the rendered PMC page and one parsed from the raw article XML, produced identical figures. The paper's own summary statement that the 50th percentile is 48.0 for men and 37.6 for women aged 20 to 29, falling to 24.4 and 18.3 at 70 to 79, matches the table below.
friend_2015_treadmill.population: 7,783 maximal treadmill CPX tests from 8 laboratories in the United States (Connecticut, Indiana, Illinois, Louisiana, Maryland, North Carolina, Tennessee, Texas), collected 2014-01-01 through 2015-02-01, in 4,611 men and 3,172 women aged 20 to 79 with no known cardiovascular disease and no known chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Maximal effort was defined as a peak respiratory exchange ratio of at least 1.0.
friend_2015_treadmill.measure: Directly measured VO2max during treadmill cardiopulmonary exercise testing.

resting_heart_rate.label: Resting heart rate
resting_heart_rate.comparability_note: This is the weak block of this file and must be labelled as such wherever it is shown. The only genuinely citable percentile table found is a seated clinic pulse count. A Garmin resting heart rate is derived from extended rest and sleep and reads systematically lower than a seated daytime pulse, so a percentile taken from this table places the athlete lower in the cohort than a like for like comparison would. Read it as a rough orientation, never as a rank.
caveats: Adult age bands in this source are 20 years wide (20-39, 40-59, 60-79, 80 and over), far coarser than the decade bands used for VO2max.

No usable published percentile table for wearable derived resting heart rate was found. Quer et al. 2020 (PLOS ONE 15(2):e0227709, 92,457 Fitbit users) reports the age and sex pattern only as a figure and publishes no numeric table by age and sex. Avram et al. 2019 (npj Digit Med 2:58, Health eHeart) reports real-world heart rate from smartphone photoplethysmography with a mean of 79.1 bpm, which is not a resting heart rate. Neither can be turned into an honest percentile table without inventing numbers, so neither is included.
The 1st percentile is absent for the 80 and over bands because the source did not calculate it.

nhanes_1999_2008_resting_pulse.name: NHANES 1999-2008 resting pulse rate reference data (CDC / NCHS)
nhanes_1999_2008_resting_pulse.citation: Ostchega Y, Porter KS, Hughes J, Dillon CF, Nwankwo T. Resting pulse rate reference data for children, adolescents, and adults: United States, 1999-2008. National Health Statistics Reports; no 41. Hyattsville, MD: National Center for Health Statistics. 2011. PMID 21905522. Tables 2 (males) and 3 (females), adult age groups only.
nhanes_1999_2008_resting_pulse.access_note: The CDC host returns HTTP 403 to automated requests. The figures here were read from the same PDF as archived by the Internet Archive at https://web.archive.org/web/2019id_/https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data/nhsr/nhsr041.pdf . The report is a United States government publication in the public domain.
nhanes_1999_2008_resting_pulse.verification: Values were parsed from the report's own tables in the PDF text layer. The report's stated adult mean of 72 bpm is consistent with the median rows below.
nhanes_1999_2008_resting_pulse.population: United States civilian noninstitutionalized population, National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 1999-2008. Of 49,114 persons examined, a normative sample of 35,302 was retained by excluding anyone with a current medical condition or medication that would affect the pulse rate, which covers pregnancy, irregular pulse, abnormal thyroid function, likely current infection and heart rate affecting prescriptions. The adult portion of that normative sample is 14,200 persons aged 20 and over. Estimates are weighted to be nationally representative.
nhanes_1999_2008_resting_pulse.measure: Resting pulse rate taken by a physician in a mobile examination centre. For participants over age 4 a radial pulse was counted manually for 30 seconds after roughly 4 minutes of seated quiet rest, then doubled to give beats per minute. No resting electrocardiogram was recorded.
